doc: What each bake is published as, read by the client for the path it
requests: `v<format>.<release>`, the format the bake was written in and
the Overture release it was baked from, as the ingest catalog names it.
A published folder is immutable, so a cache never holds a page another
replaced and going back is naming the folder before. A new release is a
new folder under the same format; a change to what a page holds or how it
is baked bumps the format. Setting a name here is the whole change.

$doc: The format each bake writes now, which a bake's folder is named by with
its release. Bumped by a change to what a page holds or how it is baked.
What the published bake declares of itself to the client: `top_level`, the
coarsest level of the pyramid it supplies whole, terrain and POI alike. The
client's floor is held there, all around the eye, and the far edge is where
that level ends (pxl-kernel world/paging/floor.rs). The dev tile server
answers the same object at the tile root's `source`, with its `--top-level`
(pxl-geo-bake bin/serve_tiles.rs); neither is guessed from what fails.
